difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 10.1.8 at source lines 339-345: for an equivalence relation (A,R) the identification type c_R(x) = c_R(y) is equivalent to R(x,y), i.e. equivalence relations are effective. The author's proof (source lines 347-361) is a full encode-decode argument rather than a citation: the relation is first extended to the quotient by double induction, which is legitimate only because the universe of propositions is a set (lines 348-354), the direction from identities to the relation is then obtained by transport after proving reflexivity (line 357), and the converse can be reduced to representatives of the quotient because the goal is a mere proposition and the quotient map is surjective (line 358), with the canonical map completing the comparison (line 359). The author notes at the end that this is the encode-decode method, which the statement does not reveal.
